title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from the previous page). S is a normal scheme of characteristic 0 (the base field may be Q), with function field K. U_S → S is a relative curve; in the genus-0 case it is P^1_S minus a divisor T'. E_K denotes the arithmetic fundamental group over the generic point, an extension of Gal(K̄/K), and E_S, E_{U_S} are the corresponding groups over S and U_S. The problem served is the 'specialisation' of sections: when does a section of the fundamental-group extension defined over the generic point K extend to a section over S? This is the section-conjecture programme of the Longue Marche notes.

Step 1 (previous page). Take a codimension-1 point x of S, so O_x is a DVR. Choose a point x̃ above x in the normalisation of O_x in K̄. Its stabiliser N_x̃ in E_K is the decomposition group, and it surjects onto Gal(\overline{k(x)}/k(x)).

Step 2 (this page). Let I_x̃ be the kernel of this surjection, the 'geometric stabiliser' or inertia group. This gives the exact sequence (7): 1 → I_x̃ → N_x̃ → Gal(\overline{k(x)}/k(x)) → 1. Because the residue characteristic is 0, all ramification is tame. Kummer theory then gives the canonical isomorphism (8): I_x̃ ≅ T_∞(\overline{k(x)}^*) ≅ T_∞(K̄^*) = Ẑ(1). The margin note 'à cause de l'hyp. de car. 0!' marks exactly this point.

Step 3. If x is the generic point of a divisor D, then k(x) is the function field of D, a field of finite type over Q. This sets up an induction on dimension within finitely generated fields.

Step 4. Grothendieck asserts that the kernel of E_K → E_S is the normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups I_x̃. Hence a homomorphism E_K → E_{U_S} (coming from a section over K) factors through E_S if and only if it vanishes ('s'annule') on each I_x̃.

Step 5. This reduces the problem to the local situation over the DVR O_x: one restricts U to U_{O_x} over Spec O_x and looks for factorisations there. The next page continues with the torsor of 'geometric' splittings under G_m(S)^∧ ≅ H^1(S,T).
errors: The claim that ker(E_K → E_S) is normally generated by the codimension-1 inertia groups is called 'immédiat', but it is Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus (SGA 1 X 3.4). Purity holds for S regular, not for S merely normal: quotient singularities give counterexamples. So one needs S regular, or else E_S must be read as classifying covers étale in codimension 1.

This is minor rather than an error: the identification (8) is canonical only as N_x̃-modules up to the Kummer choice. It also uses that the inertia group is procyclic, which is valid in residue characteristic 0 as noted in the margin.

ideas.what: Decomposition and inertia exact sequence at a codimension-1 point, with inertia ≅ Ẑ(1) via Kummer in characteristic 0
ideas.modern_name: Tame inertia / decomposition group exact sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hilbert ramification theory; Grothendieck–Murre for the tame fundamental group)

ideas.what: The kernel of Gal(K̄/K) → π_1(S) is normally generated by the inertia groups at divisors
ideas.modern_name: Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus

ideas.what: A section over the generic point extends over S iff it kills each inertia group; reduction to the DVR case Spec O_x
ideas.modern_name: Unramified sections / specialisation of Galois sections (section conjecture over function fields of finite type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discussed later by Stix, Tamagawa, Esnault–Wittenberg and others
ideas.where_published: Possibly partly in the 1983 letter to Faltings and the Esquisse; not in this form

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly plans an inductive treatment of the section conjecture over finitely generated fields. Sections over K are specialised along divisors via inertia, using that residue fields of divisors are again of finite type over Q. This is an early explicit sketch of the 'unramified sections / specialisation' approach later systematised by Stix and others, but the content on this page is standard.
missed.quote: l'hypothèse que E_K → E_{U_S} s'annule sur ledit noyau, signifie aussi qu'il s'annule sur chacun des I_x̃
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence of Grothendieck's intended reduction of the birational and finitely-generated-field section conjecture to the DVR case. It is of documentary rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is standard ramification theory and purity, applied to extending Galois sections from the generic point. It is of historical interest as a Longue Marche-era sketch, but contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 's'scinde' (twice) should read 's'annule' ('vanishes on'), which fits the logic of killing the kernel/inertia.
'dans k(x) est le corps des fonctions' should read 'donc k(x) est le corps des fonctions'.
'(... stabilisateur "géométrique"' likely reads '(ou stabilisateur "géométrique" de x̃)'; '... une suite exacte' likely 'on a une suite exacte'.
E_K should be the script $\mathcal{E}_K$ as on the previous page.
The last line likely reads 'Spec O_x, on a donc des factorisations,' rather than '... donne des factorisations'.
The margin note reads 'à cause de l'hyp. de car. 0!'.
